name: Pulihora (Andhra Tamarind Rice)
ingredients: 1 large lemon-sized ball of Tamarind (soaked in warm water)
instructions: Cook rice until grains are fluffy and distinct; spread onto a wide tray with 1 tbsp sesame oil and turmeric powder to cool.
Extract thick tamarind pulp from soaked tamarind with 1 cup of warm water.
In a heavy pan, simmer the tamarind pulp with slit green chilies, salt, and turmeric until it thickens into a glossy paste.
In a separate pan, heat oil and roast peanuts until crunchy. Add mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, dried red chilies, hing, and fresh curry leaves.
Combine the thickened tamarind paste with the cooled rice gently, then pour the hot tempering over it and mix thoroughly.
Let the pulihora rest for at least 1 hour so the aromatic flavors infuse deeply before serving.

name: Bamboo Shoot Stir Fry
ingredients: 250g Fresh or Fermented Tender Bamboo Shoots (thinly sliced)
Fresh Coriander or indigenous herbs for garnish
instructions: Boil sliced bamboo shoots in salted water for 10-15 minutes to eliminate natural bitterness, then drain thoroughly.
Heat mustard oil in a cast-iron wok until it begins to smoke gently, then lower heat.
Add fenugreek seeds and crushed garlic; sauté until aromatic and golden.
Add sliced onions and green chilies, cooking until onions turn translucent.
Stir in the drained bamboo shoots, turmeric powder, and salt. Sauté on medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh herbs and serve hot alongside steamed sticky rice.

name: Assamese Duck Meat Curry (Kumura Dha)
ingredients: 800g Fresh Duck Meat (cut into bone-in curry pieces)
300g White Gourd / Ash Gourd (Kumura), peeled and cubed
3 Green Cardamom pods and 1 inch Cinnamon
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed kadhai until smoking point, then add bay leaves, cardamom, and cinnamon.
Add sliced onions and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook out the raw aroma.
Add the duck meat, turmeric, salt, and cumin powder. Cook on high heat for 10 minutes until meat browns.
Lower heat, cover tightly, and allow duck to cook in its own juices for 20 minutes.
Add cubed ash gourd and freshly crushed black pepper; toss well to coat.
Pour in 2 cups of warm water, cover, and slow-cook until duck meat is fork-tender and curry is thick.
Serve piping hot with fragrant Joha rice.

name: Bihari Litti Chokha
ingredients: 4 Green Chilies and 1 inch Ginger (finely chopped)
instructions: Knead a firm, pliable dough using wheat flour, a pinch of salt, 1 tsp oil, and water. Rest for 20 minutes.
For filling: Mix sattu with chopped green chilies, ginger, coriander, ajwain, kalonji, lemon juice, mustard oil, and salt with a splash of water until moist.
Form dough into smooth lemon-sized balls, cup them into hollow pockets, fill generously with sattu mixture, and seal tight.
Bake littis on a charcoal grill, tandoor, or preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, turning periodically until outer crust is charred and crisp.
For chokha: Roast brinjal and tomatoes on open flame until skins are charred. Peel and mash together with boiled potatoes, raw mustard oil, chopped onions, green chilies, and salt.
Dip hot littis generously in melted desi ghee, crack them open slightly, and serve alongside smoky chokha.

name: Chhattisgarhi Steamed Muthia
ingredients: 1/2 cup Chopped Fresh Fenugreek (Methi) or Spinach
instructions: Combine rice flour, mashed rice, chopped greens, salt, turmeric, and warm water to form a soft dough.
Pinch small portions of dough and shape into cylindrical muthia rolls using your fingers.
Grease a steamer plate and steam muthias for 12-15 minutes until firm to the touch.
Heat oil in a wide pan; crackle mustard seeds, sesame seeds, dried chilies, and curry leaves.
Add steamed muthias to the tempering and pan-fry on medium heat until surfaces turn lightly golden and crisp.
Serve warm with spicy green coriander chutney.

name: Goan Fish Curry (Xitt Codi)
ingredients: 1 tbsp Coriander Seeds & 1 tsp Cumin Seeds
4-5 Dried Kokum petals (soaked in warm water)
instructions: Grind grated coconut, Kashmiri chilies, coriander seeds, cumin, garlic, ginger, and turmeric into a silky smooth paste with a little water.
Heat coconut oil in an earthenware pot (matka); add slit green chilies and the ground spice paste. Sauté gently until oil separates.
Add 1.5 cups of water and soaked kokum with its water; bring the curry to a gentle simmer.
Gently slide in fish fillets and coconut milk; simmer on low heat for 6-8 minutes without stirring vigorously to avoid breaking the fish.
Season with salt and let rest for 15 minutes before serving with hot steamed Goan red rice.

name: Khaman Dhokla
ingredients: 1 tsp Eno Fruit Salt or Baking Soda
For tempering: 1 tbsp Oil, 1 tsp Mustard Seeds, 1 tbsp Sesame Seeds, 4 Slit Green Chilies, 1 sprig Curry Leaves, 1/2 cup Water with 1 tsp Sugar
Garnish: Fresh grated coconut and coriander
instructions: Whisk besan, sooji, turmeric, ginger-chili paste, lemon juice, sugar, salt, and water into a smooth, lump-free batter.
Grease a steaming tin and boil water in the steamer.
Right before pouring, stir in Eno fruit salt and 1 tsp water; whisk in one direction until batter doubles in volume and becomes airy.
Pour immediately into the tin and steam on high heat for 18-20 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
In a small pan, prepare tempering by crackling mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, and green chilies in oil, then pour in sugar water.
Cut steamed dhokla into neat squares, pour the warm tempering water evenly to keep it moist, and garnish with coconut and coriander.

name: Haryanvi Bajra Khichdi
ingredients: 1 cup Pearl Millet (Bajra), crushed or coarsely ground
instructions: Pound bajra lightly in a mortar or pulse coarsely in a blender, then husk to remove chaff.
Wash bajra and moong dal together thoroughly.
In a heavy pot or pressure cooker, bring water to a boil, then add the bajra and dal mixture with salt and turmeric.
Cook on low heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until grains are thoroughly soft and porridge-like (about 4 whistles in pressure cooker).
Heat ghee, temper with cumin seeds and hing, and stir into the hot khichdi.
Serve piping hot with fresh curd, jaggery, and extra spoons of golden ghee.

name: Himachali Dham (Madra)
ingredients: 1.5 cups Soaked Red Kidney Beans (Rajma) or Chickpeas (Kabuli Chana)
instructions: Pressure cook soaked rajma in water with a pinch of salt until tender.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy brass or iron pan until smoky; add whole cardamoms, cinnamon, and cloves.
Lower heat and add whisked yogurt gradually, stirring continuously on low heat to prevent curdling.
Add turmeric, dry ginger powder, and fennel powder. Sauté until oil separates from yogurt gravy.
Add boiled beans along with a cup of cooking liquid. Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes until gravy thickens.
Garnish with fried cashews and raisins. Serve warm with steamed basmati rice.

name: Jharkhandi Dhooska
instructions: Wash and soak rice, chana dal, and urad dal together in water for 4-5 hours.
Drain and grind into a thick, smooth pouring batter with green chilies, ginger, and minimal water.
Stir in cumin seeds, turmeric, hing, and salt. Whisk vigorously for 3 minutes to aerate.
Heat oil in a deep kadhai on medium heat.
Pour a small ladle of batter directly into the center without stirring; it will puff up like a poori.
Flip and fry until both sides are crisp and golden brown.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot with spicy aloo-chana sabzi.

name: Karnataka Bisi Bele Bath
ingredients: 1.5 cups Diced Mixed Vegetables (Carrot, Beans, Peas, Shallots)
3 tbsp Bisi Bele Bath Masala Powder
1 tsp Mustard Seeds & 2 dried red chilies
instructions: Pressure cook rice and toor dal together with 4 cups water and turmeric until very soft.
In a pot, boil mixed vegetables in tamarind extract and salt until tender.
Dissolve Bisi Bele Bath powder in 1/2 cup water and stir into the simmering vegetables.
Add cooked rice and dal mixture; stir well, adding warm water to achieve a rich, semi-thick consistency.
Heat ghee in a pan, fry cashews, mustard seeds, red chilies, and curry leaves until fragrant.
Pour hot tempering over the bath, stir well, and serve hot with potato chips or boondi raita.

name: Kerala Appam with Stew
ingredients: For Stew: 2 cups Mixed Vegetables, 1.5 cups Thin Coconut Milk, 1/2 cup Thick Coconut Milk, Whole Spices, Green Chilies, Coconut Oil, Curry Leaves
instructions: Grind soaked rice, grated coconut, and cooked rice with water into a smooth batter.
Dissolve yeast and sugar in 2 tbsp warm water, mix into batter, and ferment for 8 hours until frothy.
Add salt and a pinch of sugar; batter should be of pouring consistency.
Heat an appachatti (curved appam pan). Pour a ladle of batter into the center, swirl the pan to coat sides, cover, and steam on medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
The edges will turn golden and crisp while center remains fluffy.
For stew: Simmer vegetables with whole spices, green chilies, and thin coconut milk until soft, then finish with thick coconut milk and curry leaves tempered in coconut oil.
Serve warm appams with aromatic stew.

name: Bhutte Ka Kees
ingredients: 1 tsp Mustard Seeds & 1 tsp Cumin Seeds
2 tbsp Fresh Grated Coconut and Coriander
instructions: Grate the fresh corn cobs on a medium box grater, reserving all milky juice.
Heat ghee in a pan; add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and hing.
Add minced green chilies and ginger; sauté for 1 minute.
Add grated corn, turmeric, red chili powder, and salt. Sauté on medium heat for 5 minutes.
Pour in milk slowly, stirring continuously to prevent scorching. Cover and simmer on low heat for 10-12 minutes until corn absorbs milk and thickens.
Finish with fresh lemon juice, grated coconut, and coriander leaves. Serve warm.

name: Kolhapuri Misal Pav
ingredients: 2 tbsp Misal Masala (or Kolhapuri Kanda-Lasun Masala)
3 tbsp Oil (essential for fiery 'tarri' oil layer)
1 tsp Mustard Seeds & 1 sprig Curry Leaves
For assembly: 1 cup Spicy Farsan / Chiwda, Chopped Raw Onions, Lemon wedges, Coriander, 8 Buttered Pav buns
instructions: Boil sprouted matki with a pinch of turmeric and salt until just cooked but holding shape; drain and reserve liquid.
Heat oil generously in a kadhai; add mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add onions and sauté until deep golden brown, then add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes until mushy.
Add misal masala, red chili powder, and salt. Cook until bright red oil ('tarri') floats on top.
Add boiled sprouts and 3 cups of water; simmer vigorously for 15 minutes to form rich spicy gravy.
Assembly: Ladle sprouts into bowls, top generously with spicy farsan and fresh onions, pour thin fiery tarri over, and serve with warm buttered pav and lemon.

name: Manipuri Kangshoi
ingredients: 200g Seasonal Green Vegetables (Mustard greens, Spinach, Cabbage)
3-4 Fresh Green Chilies or King Chili (slit)
2 tbsp Roasted Ngari (fermented fish paste) or dried shiitake for vegetarian version
instructions: Bring 3 cups of water to a rolling boil in a deep soup pot.
Add sliced onions, crushed ginger, slit chilies, turmeric, salt, and roasted ngari or mushroom.
Add sliced potatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until partially tender.
Add seasonal greens and vegetables; cook on medium heat for 6-8 minutes without covering so greens retain color.
Turn off heat and let steep for 3 minutes.
Serve warm as a light, revitalizing soup alongside steamed rice.

name: Khasi Jadoh
ingredients: 2 cups Hill Red Rice (Joha or indigenous red rice)
2 tbsp Ginger paste & 1 tbsp Garlic paste
2 tbsp Black Sesame Seeds (roasted and powdered)
instructions: Wash red rice and soak in water for 20 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot; add bay leaves and chopped onions until translucent.
Add ginger and garlic pastes; sauté until fragrant.
Add meat pieces and cook on medium heat until lightly browned.
Stir in roasted black sesame powder, green chilies, and salt; mix thoroughly with meat.
Add drained red rice and roast for 2 minutes.
Add 4 cups of boiling water, cover tightly, reduce heat, and cook until rice is tender and moisture absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, fluff with fork, and serve.

name: Mizo Misa Mach Poora
instructions: Marinate cleaned prawns with turmeric, crushed garlic, green chilies, pepper, lime juice, and salt for 15 minutes.
Toss with cold-pressed mustard oil.
For authentic flavor, wrap marinated prawns inside softened banana leaf packets.
Roast over glowing charcoal or grill in a cast-iron skillet on medium heat for 6-8 minutes per side.
Unwrap and serve hot with steamed rice and boiled mountain greens.

name: Naga Pork with Bamboo Shoot
ingredients: 600g Pork belly or shoulder (cut into bite-sized cubes)
3 tbsp Fermented Bamboo Shoot (wet or dry)
2 Naga King Chilies (Bhut Jolokia) or 6 Dry Red Chilies
instructions: Place pork cubes into a heavy pot without oil; render over medium heat until natural pork fat releases.
Add crushed garlic, ginger, and bruised king chili; sauté in the rendered fat for 3 minutes.
Add fermented bamboo shoot and salt. Mix thoroughly to allow deep aromas to permeate.
Pour in 1.5 cups of warm water, cover with heavy lid, and simmer on gentle heat for 35-40 minutes until pork is meltingly tender.
Uncover and reduce gravy to a thick, glossy coat around the meat.
Serve warm with plain sticky rice.

name: Odisha Chhena Poda
ingredients: 500g Fresh Chhena (Paneer curd, moist and freshly made)
3/4 cup Fine Sugar (plus 2 tbsp for caramelizing)
Sal or Banana leaves for lining baking tin
instructions: Knead fresh chhena by hand for 6-8 minutes until soft and creamy, without making it greasy.
Add sugar, sooji, cardamom powder, melted ghee, cashews, and raisins. Mix gently into a smooth batter.
In a baking pan or cake tin, caramelize 2 tbsp sugar with a drop of ghee over low flame until golden amber.
Line the tin with ghee-brushed banana leaves, pour chhena batter, and smooth the top.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 45-55 minutes until the crust turns dark golden brown and caramelizes.
Cool completely before slicing into triangles to appreciate the smoky, sweet caramelized crust.

name: Makki di Roti & Sarson da Saag
ingredients: 3 tbsp Makki Atta (Cornmeal, for saag thickening)
2 cups Makki Atta (Cornmeal flour, for roti)
4 tbsp Desi Ghee (plus extra for serving)
Fresh White Butter (Makhan) and Jaggery for serving
instructions: Wash greens thoroughly, chop roughly, and pressure cook with ginger, garlic, green chilies, and salt with 1 cup water for 15 minutes.
Blend or mash cooked greens coarsely with a wooden churner (madhani).
Dissolve makki atta in water, stir into the greens, and simmer for 20 minutes on low heat until creamy.
In a separate pan, prepare tadka with ghee, sliced onions, tomatoes, and red chili powder; fold into the simmering saag.
For roti: Knead makki atta with warm water into soft dough. Pat gently between damp palms or parchment paper into round flatbreads.
Cook on a medium hot tawa with generous ghee until golden speckled on both sides.
Serve piping hot with a dollop of white butter (makhan) and jaggery.

name: Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma
ingredients: 2 cups Coarse Whole Wheat Flour (Gehu ka atta)
1/4 cup Melted Desi Ghee (Moyen for dough)
1/4 tsp Baking Soda and Salt to taste
1/4 cup each Toor, Chana, Moong, Urad, and Masoor Dals (Panchmel Dal)
1 tsp Cumin Seeds and 1/4 tsp Asafoetida (Hing)
1 tsp Red Chili Powder, Coriander Powder, and Garam Masala
1/2 cup Powdered Sugar or Boora (for Churma)
1 cup Pure Desi Ghee (for dipping and serving)
instructions: Mix wheat flour, sooji, ajwain, salt, baking soda, and ghee until it resembles breadcrumbs. Knead a tight dough with warm water.
Divide into balls, make a gentle indentation in the center, and bake in a tandoor or 200°C oven for 30 minutes until cracked and golden.
Boil the 5 dals with turmeric and salt until tender. Prepare a rich ghee tadka with cumin, hing, green chilies, tomatoes, and spices; stir into dal.
For churma: Crush 2 hot baatis in a food processor, sift, and mix with ghee, powdered sugar, cardamom, and sliced almonds.
Dip hot baatis in a bowl of melted desi ghee, crush lightly into warm spicy dal, and enjoy with sweet churma.

name: Sikkimese Steamed Momos
ingredients: 2 cups Finely Minced Cabbage, Carrots, Onions, and Spring Onions (or Minced Meat)
For Chutney: 4 Dry Red Chilies, 2 Tomatoes, 4 Garlic cloves boiled and blended
instructions: Knead flour and water into a smooth, pliable dough. Cover with damp cloth for 30 minutes.
Sauté vegetables or meat filling with ginger, garlic, soy sauce, pepper, butter, and salt on high heat for 2 minutes to keep crisp.
Roll dough into thin 3-inch circular wrappers with edges slightly thinner than the center.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center, pleat the edges around the filling, and pinch closed into classic crescent or round shape.
Grease steamer racks, arrange momos leaving space between them, and steam over rolling boiling water for 10-12 minutes until translucent.
Serve hot with spicy garlic-chili tomato dip and clear soup.

name: Tamil Ven Pongal
instructions: Dry roast moong dal in a pan on medium heat until fragrant and slightly golden, then wash with rice.
Pressure cook rice and dal in water and milk with salt and ginger for 4-5 whistles until very soft and creamy.
Gently mash cooked pongal with the back of a ladle.
Heat ghee in a pan, fry cashews until golden, then add cumin seeds, whole peppercorns, hing, and curry leaves.
Pour hot sizzling tempering over the mashed pongal and fold in gently.
Serve piping hot with fresh coconut chutney and spicy vegetable sambar.

name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
ingredients: 3 cups Aged Long Grain Basmati Rice (soaked 30 mins)
800g Chicken or Lamb (marinated with yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chili, garam masala, mint, coriander, and fried onions)
Whole Spices (Shahi jeera, star anise, cardamom, mace, cinnamon, cloves)
Whole Wheat Dough to seal the pot
instructions: Marinate meat for at least 2 hours with yogurt, biryani spices, ginger-garlic paste, fresh herbs, and salt.
Boil water with whole spices and salt; cook soaked basmati rice until 70% done, then drain immediately.
In a thick-bottomed handi, layer marinated meat at the base.
Spread the 70% cooked rice evenly over the meat.
Top with fried onions, saffron milk, chopped mint, coriander, and generous spoons of ghee.
Seal the rim with wheat dough and cover tightly with a heavy lid.
Cook on high heat for 10 minutes, then place on a hot iron tawa on low heat for 35 minutes (dum).
Rest for 15 minutes before unsealing. Gently fluff layers to reveal aromatic long rice and tender meat, served with mirchi ka salan and dahi raita.

name: Tripuri Chakhwi
ingredients: 1/2 tsp Baking Soda or traditional Khar (alkaline extract)
Rice flour paste (1 tbsp in water)
instructions: Bring 3 cups of water to a boil in a pan.
Add baking soda or indigenous khar along with green chilies, ginger, and salt.
Add bamboo shoots, raw papaya cubes, and jackfruit seeds.
Simmer on medium heat for 15-20 minutes until papaya is completely tender.
Stir in rice flour slurry to impart gentle thickness to the clear aromatic broth.
Serve warm as a nourishing digestive with steamed rice.

name: Lucknowi Tunday Kababi
ingredients: 500g Finely Minced Meat (passed through mincer 4 times)
1 tbsp Special Potli Masala (Cardamom, mace, nutmeg, clove, star anise, rose petals, black pepper)
Live charcoal and ghee for smoking (dhungar)
instructions: Marinate finely ground meat with raw papaya paste and salt for 1 hour.
Add roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, and aromatic potli spice blend; knead thoroughly for 5 minutes until soft and cohesive.
Place a small metal bowl in the meat, add hot charcoal, pour 1 tsp ghee, and cover tightly for 10 minutes to infuse smoky aroma.
Shape meat into flat patties with oiled hands.
Heat ghee on a flat tawa; pan-fry kebabs on medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until beautifully browned.
Serve hot with roomali roti, sliced minty onions, and lemon wedges.

name: Uttarakhandi Kafuli
ingredients: 2 tbsp Rice Flour (dissolved in 1/2 cup water)
1/2 tsp Jakhiya (wild mustard) or Cumin Seeds
instructions: Wash greens thoroughly and boil in water with green chilies, ginger, and salt until tender.
Mash greens into a smooth purée using a blender or traditional wooden churner.
Heat mustard oil in an iron kadhai until smoking point.
Add jakhiya seeds and crushed garlic; fry until crisp and fragrant.
Pour in greens purée, turmeric, and hing. Bring to a gentle boil.
Pour in rice flour slurry while stirring continuously; simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until thick and velvet-smooth.
Serve piping hot with steamed rice or madua (ragi) rotis.

name: Bengali Kosha Mangsho
ingredients: 1 tbsp Kashmiri Chili Powder & 1 tsp Turmeric
Whole Spices: 2 Bay leaves, 4 Cardamom, 1 inch Cinnamon, 4 Cloves
1 tsp Sugar (caramelized for rich dark color)
instructions: Marinate mutton with yogurt, 1 tbsp mustard oil, turmeric, and red chili powder for 2 hours.
Heat remaining mustard oil in a heavy kadhai until smoking; add 1 tsp sugar and allow to caramelize into deep golden brown.
Add whole spices and sliced onions; sauté patiently on medium heat until dark mahogany brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook out raw aroma. Add marinated mutton and fry on medium-high heat for 15 minutes.
Cover and 'koshano' (slow roast-fry) on low flame, stirring every 5 minutes until meat turns deep dark brown and oil releases cleanly.
Add fried potato halves and 1.5 cups warm water; simmer on low heat until mutton is melt-in-mouth tender and gravy is thick and clinging to meat.
Serve hot with fluffy luchi, Bengali sweet pulao, or steamed rice.
